buildings.cite: The airfield schema needs at least one strike target. The Army history says the field was overgrown and unoccupied, not that nothing was prepared; one grown-over dispersal bay, outside the open drop-zone ground, is the least-invented thing that satisfies the schema.

f3-site-lock.claim: Canonical site-state lock: ownership, readiness, construction, damage and clutter per window

army-leyte-ch8.claim: Burauen airfields: San Pablo about 5 mi west of Dulag, 2 mi east of Burauen, east-west, 164 x 4,920 ft, overgrown and unoccupied; Bayug just north of the highway, a half mile east of Burauen, about 5,000 ft; Buri about 1 mi northeast of Burauen, east-west, 5,000 ft, the most important of the three

army-leyte-ch11.claim: Mud and field construction problems; Buri and San Pablo abandoned, Bayug work continued (late Nov 1944)

army-leyte-ch17.claim: Operation Te-Go: attacks on the Buri and San Pablo airfields on 6-7 Dec 1944

marine-aviation-philippines.claim: Tacloban and Dulag construction problems; Tanauan work after 28 Nov; the inland fields abandoned

reference.source: Runway width and length are the Army history (ch. VIII: east-west, 164 x 4,920 ft = 50 x 1,500 m, overgrown, unoccupied by the Japanese, 2 mi east of Burauen); center and heading 80 are FITTED to the shipped terrain near that offset (tools/sites/surveyStrip.ts, 2026-10-17): all land, about 4 m of relief over 1.5 km. The base has ONE building, a grown-over dispersal revetment the schema one-target minimum forces (its placement cite says so); nothing else stood here before the invasion, and every other structure arrives in the window that builds it (`added`). The clearing is 760 x 1,700 m of open ground around the strip, the J5/J6 drop zone; no building stands inside its central 400 m (a test pins that). There is no "overgrown weeds" clutter kind, so the overgrown pre-invasion field is shown by absence. Windows follow the F3 section 5 San Pablo row; the endgame is serviceable and the alternate is not (F8 plan, F8B detail, ruling 3).

pre-invasion.note: Overgrown with weeds and unoccupied by the Japanese (Army ch. VIII).
